verificationNotes: All interfaces, endpoint gateways, server VLAN and router IPv6 forwarding are ready. Only R2 starts with remote routes. R1 and R3 need the published commands.

SRV1 host entries (/32 and /128) at AD 200 are installed alongside broader server-network entries (/24 and /64) at AD 1. Packet events verify R1 Gi0/2 for SRV1 and Gi0/1 through R2 for adjacent SRV2. AD does not override longest-prefix matching.
R3 return routes use the direct link to R1, so SRV2 request/reply paths are asymmetric. Traceroute reply source addresses may identify that return-facing R3 interface.
Removing each host route preserves replies through the broader route but revokes the corresponding configuration task. No new default or floating route is involved.
The completed reference has four configuration goals and no fabricated echo credit; six real traffic checks are needed for all ten tasks.
The browser workflow opens PC1 Desktop → Command prompt for traceroute and verifies actual R2 presence or absence for both servers in both address families.

The isolated repeat’s 35,885-byte saved state validated and restored all ten tasks in the simulator; that browser run also passed. All eight new-lab browser checks and seven general catalog checks passed. The final rebuilt index.html and dist/index.html match the frozen offline browser input byte for byte. Light desktop topology and light/dark 320px guides were visually reviewed.
